doc.title: Urbie Green interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Settling in New York and playing 'actor' in the studios
summary: After eleven years on the road he settles in New York; studio work meant imitating Dorsey or Teagarden, even a dog eating dog food.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: You did some pretty extensive studio work over the years. Was that mostly in New York?
Yeah, after eleven years of traveling around with bands I finally settled down in New York.
Can you tell us about was there any studio things that you remember that bordered on the ridiculous?
Or anything that was funny, or just little quirky things about jazz?

When I listen to music behind some commercials these days I’m thinking, you know, people had to actually play this. And someone sat down and wrote this thing. And I’m wondering sometimes how some of the players keep a straight face.

Well in the studio sometimes you get in a situation where you kind of have to be an actor, like you’re not really playing yourself, when you’re choosing — I mean I’m talking about musical acting. Like they’d say, “play this like Tommy Dorsey,” or you know, so you’d try to play, there was only one Tommy Dorsey, so you do something similar to that. Or, “Jack Teagarden I wrote this for.” One time I had to imitate a dog eating dog food [scats]. I guess that’s really, what’s I can’t think, I’ve got a small vocabulary. Never went to no college, you know.
